findings.where: First screen (hero) at 1440 and 390: the space at the foot of the framed sheet, below the supporting paragraph, where the palette and texture notes place the pad-yellow address strip
findings.fault: The first screen has no action at all. The address strip that the palette and texture notes describe is not in the layout: the sheet ends after the supporting paragraph, and nothing in the hero shows Mark's address or a way to reach him. The parts map agrees, since no contact link exists anywhere on the page. The hero has his line and his photograph, but nothing to do next.
findings.who_objects: A development bank officer who has read Mark's line and wants to contact him finds no address and no contact link, only Profile, Articles and Blog. The founder judges this screen first, against a brief that requires one direct, personal way to reach Mark, with the address shown.

findings.where: Article specimen, the Download block, at the point where it meets the Motion panel (1440 and 390)
findings.fault: The PDF entry runs into the Motion panel with no gap. At 1440 the panel's top edge sits about 15 px under the link's second line. At 390 the 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line touches the panel. Every other section is separated by a large gap, so this one break in the rhythm makes the Download entry look cut off, as if it belonged to the panel.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article specimen, who cannot tell where the article ends. The founder, judging whether the PDF list reads as 'the product', sees it squeezed against an unrelated block.

findings.where: Motion panel at 1440: the panel's box and its 'Motion' label, compared with the Palette, Type pair, Texture and Article page sections above it
findings.fault: Breaks continuity and common region. Every other section hangs its label on one left edge (about x 170) with content on a second edge (about x 426). The Motion panel is a filled box spanning 170 to 1270, which pushes its label to 194 and its content to 450. Both alignment lines step inwards, and the motion sketch reads as a separate inserted card, not as part of the same sheet.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing the style tile's parts. The motion sketch looks bolted on and pulls the eye more than the article it follows.

findings.where: Motion panel at 390: the timing table (Element, Start, Length, Easing)
findings.fault: The four-column table is kept at phone width, so the Element column gets about 60 px. Its descriptions wrap one or two words per line ('Hold: / the / sheet is / already…'), and one row runs to eleven lines while the number columns stand mostly empty beside it.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reviewing the tile on a phone, the founder included. The timing description becomes a column of fragments that is tiring to read.

findings.where: Palette row (1440 and 390): the four swatches
findings.fault: The swatches break similarity. One is an outlined rectangle, one has rounded corners, one is an oval and one has a blue border. Four items of the same kind, with labels set identically, take four different shapes, so the row looks like it is showing different kinds of object rather than four colours of one system.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the palette. The mixed shapes suggest that corner radius, ovals and blue borders are part of the look, which contradicts the 'square at every corner' hairline the texture note sets out.
